questions.prompt: Why is the tool/call event logged before the pre-execute hook runs?
options: So the request is recorded even if something later crashes or denies it
Because hooks read the call from the log
Because the model needs the event before the tool runs
So the log can be sorted by tool name
questions.explanation: Logging first means every request leaves a record, and every path through the pipeline also ends by logging its result.

questions.prompt: No plugin listens on tools/pre-execute. What does the hook return for a call?
options: An error saying no listeners are registered
allow, because the innermost action returns allow
questions.explanation: The waterfall runs the innermost action when there are no listeners, and that action answers allow.

questions.prompt: A plugin wants to change a run_command call's command before it runs. Why does the pipeline not allow this?
options: Because waterfall hooks cannot see arguments
Because the logged arguments, the ones on screen and the ones executed must be the same
Because commands are read-only strings in TypeScript
questions.explanation: If a hook rewrote arguments, the log and the screen would show one command while another actually ran. Hooks may block or replace results instead.
